try-the-manual-controls.text: The simulator has two explicit profiles. The first-release naming profile lets you queue and cancel an unfulfilled claim, exercise each cancellation refusal, queue competing claims, fold the winner, observe the duplicate refusal, resolve the certified fixture, and try a refused Delete. The generic registry profile separately demonstrates Insert withdrawal, address evolution, retirement, Delete, and batch ordering. Neither profile silently falls back to the other.

Naming claim cancellation requires separate approval and copies the refund address stored in the request; redirect, certification-only, post-fold, and replay attempts are refused. The playable active-name lifecycle maintains a payment destination, recovers through a committed next controller, and queues then separately completes retirement through either the controller or quorum route. Retirement request withdrawal is a separate refused attempt. The generic profile retains its own Insert withdrawal journey.

what-the-evidence-establishes.text: This simulator candidate replays fifty-eight generic Lean rows, thirty-four naming rows, and forty-three lifecycle and wire rows. Forty-one generic declarations and seventeen naming declarations are proved from the standard axioms. The lifecycle denominator covers pending-claim cancellation, maintenance, recovery, retirement, resolution, initialization, re-registration, and the exact four-field datum. The generic ledger has twelve controlled checks, seventeen exhibits only, and twelve gaps; naming has fifteen controlled checks, two exhibits only, and no gaps. These are finite checks, not acceptance.

model-and-assumptions.text: The generic model uses tagged commitments and logical lists for maps and UTxOs. Application acceptance and witnesses are supplied evidence; scripts and signatures are not verified here. Generic refund values are commitments rather than modeled payments. The naming fixture uses canonical binary Cardano addresses, a thirty-two-byte next-controller commitment, and a threshold quorum. The browser drives those shapes through the integrated lifecycle transition, but this does not establish compiled-script interoperability or ledger execution.

reproduce-the-focused-checks.text: In a source checkout, use the simulator build check, Node gate, self-test, lifecycle gate, and both browser checks. For archive evidence, first verify the internal checksum manifest, then run the check app from the archive's own locked flake. It compiles the shipped Lean model, regenerates all corpora, checks compiled axioms, verifies both public pages, replays generic, naming, lifecycle, and wire rows, and executes negative controls. The locked toolchain may be acquired when uncached, but model and replay inputs never come from a checkout or unpinned fetch. This remains review material, not a published release or ledger artifact.
